Background Requirements

The official Italian Consulate General requirement — as stated on the esteri.it government portal — specifies a white background. White is the safest and universally accepted choice across all Italian questure and consulates. Some questure may accept a very light, uniform grey for improved contrast with fair skin, but this is not guaranteed across all offices. Patterned, coloured, or shaded backgrounds — including shadows falling on the background behind the head — will result in rejection. For best results, stand at least one metre in front of a plain white wall and use diffused, even lighting to prevent the shadow behind the head that is the most common cause of background rejection in Italy.

Print Quality and Paper Type

Italian authorities are strict about print quality. The Polizia di Stato requires that photos be printed on high-quality photographic paper — matte or semi-matte finish is standard and preferred; some questure have rejected photos printed on glossy paper when glare affects legibility. The photo must be sharp, correctly exposed, and free of pixelation, blur, or visible inkjet dots. Damaged, creased, folded, or ink-marked photos are rejected. Our digital file is calibrated for 300 DPI professional lab printing, ensuring the final print meets the Polizia di Stato's high standards.

Facial Expression, Head Position, and Gaze

The Italian fototessera requires a neutral expression with the mouth closed. Smiling, frowning, or any exaggerated expression is not permitted, as the ICAO biometric standard requires the face to be in its resting, everyday position for reliable facial recognition. The face must be fully forward-facing — no tilt, no rotation to either side. Both eyes must be open and clearly visible, looking directly into the camera. The face must be fully visible without any part obscured by hair, accessories, or shadows. The photo must accurately reflect your current appearance.

Glasses, Accessories, and Clothing

The Polizia di Stato now actively discourages glasses in passport photos to avoid glare and shadow issues that can cause biometric scanning failures. While this is not an absolute ban, removing glasses is the safest approach. Sunglasses and tinted lenses are never permitted under any circumstance. Hats and head coverings are generally not allowed; exceptions exist for documented religious or medical reasons, in which case the face must still be fully visible and an appropriate supporting statement may be required. Everyday clothing is recommended — avoid white or very light-coloured tops, which can blend into the white background, and avoid uniforms or costumes. Jewellery and facial piercings are permitted as long as they do not obscure any part of the face.

Photo Recency and Current Appearance

The photo must have been taken within the last six months and must accurately reflect your current appearance. Italian consulates are particularly strict about this rule — even if a photo is within the six-month window, a significant change in hairstyle, hair colour, or facial hair may prompt a request for a newer photo to ensure the document accurately identifies the holder.

Children and Infants

The same fototessera specifications apply to children and infants. Only the child should appear in the photo — no parent, carer, or other person may be visible. Baby equipment, toys, and car seats must not appear. For infants who cannot hold their heads independently, laying them on a plain white or off-white surface works well; ensure no shadows fall across the face. Infants' eyes do not need to be fully open, but all other rules apply.

Evita Code e Rifiuti alla Questura

Securing a passport appointment at an Italian questura can take several months in 2026. A rejected photo wastes that appointment entirely. Our AI tool automatically crops your face to the 32–36 mm biometric zone within the 35×45 mm fototessera frame, sets a clean white background, and delivers a 300 DPI JPEG ready for professional printing — meeting the standards of the Polizia di Stato and the Ministero dell'Interno on the first attempt.

These rules apply to every Italian short-stay Schengen visa (Type C) and long-stay national visa (Type D) application, whether submitted at an Italian Consulate, a VFS Global visa application centre, or via the Italian online pre-application portal. As confirmed on the official Italian Consulate General website (esteri.it), the photo for a Schengen visa application must be a recent passport-style photograph measuring 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm with a white background and full front view. Non-compliant photos are rejected without exception at the application stage.

Official Photo Dimensions and Technical Specifications

The required photo size for an Italian Schengen visa is 35 mm wide by 45 mm tall — the universal Schengen format. The face, measured from the bottom of the chin to the top of the crown, must be between 32 mm and 36 mm, placing it within the 70 to 80 percent biometric zone of the photo height. This is the same specification used across all 29 Schengen member states and is non-negotiable. The US 2×2 inch format is a different shape and size, and will not be accepted at Italian consulates. For in-person applications, the photo must be printed in full colour on high-quality photographic paper. The Italian Consulate General specifies a white background for Schengen visa photos — this is the officially stated requirement on the esteri.it government portal. White is the universally accepted background colour across all 29 Schengen states and eliminates any risk of rejection on background grounds. Some guidance materials reference light grey as an acceptable alternative for contrast purposes, but white remains the stated standard. The background must be completely uniform — no gradients, shadows, patterns, or visible objects behind the subject are permitted. A shadow falling behind the head from poor lighting is one of the most frequent rejection causes and is entirely avoidable with correct positioning and diffused lighting.

Expression, Head Position, and Gaze

All Schengen visa photos must comply with ICAO biometric positioning standards. The face must be fully forward-facing with no tilt or rotation to either side. The expression must be completely neutral with the mouth closed — even a slight smile can be grounds for rejection at Italian consulates, which are among the stricter Schengen posts in Europe. Both eyes must be open, fully visible, and looking directly into the camera. The face must not be obscured by hair, accessories, or shadows. There must be no red-eye effect.

Glasses and Accessories

Sunglasses and tinted lenses are never permitted in Schengen visa photos. Clear prescription glasses are technically not banned under Schengen rules, but Italy allows them only if there is no glare, no shadow, and no heavy frame obscuring the eyes. Given that glare and shadow from glasses are common causes of biometric rejection, removing glasses entirely is the most reliable approach. Hats and head coverings are not permitted except for documented religious or medical reasons, and even then the full face must remain clearly visible.

Clothing and Colour Contrast

Everyday clothing is required — uniforms, costumes, and official-looking attire must not be worn. Avoid white and very light-coloured clothing, as these can blend into the white background and reduce the contrast needed for biometric processing. Dark clothing provides the best contrast against a white background. Jewellery is permitted as long as it does not obstruct any part of the face.

Number of Prints and Submission

For in-person Schengen visa applications at Italian consulates or VFS Global centres, two identical printed photographs from the same session are required. The photos must be printed on professional photographic paper — unmarked on both sides, free of creases, tears, or damage, and unaltered by computer software or filters. Photos from different sessions, even if taken on the same day, are not considered identical and may be rejected.

Visa Information System (VIS) Compliance

Your Schengen visa photo is enrolled into the European Visa Information System (VIS), where it is retained for five years alongside fingerprint biometrics. The VIS runs automated facial recognition checks against each uploaded image, which is why sharpness, correct exposure, and accurate colour rendering are technically essential — not just cosmetic preferences. Blurry, dark, or incorrectly exposed photos fail VIS enrolment and result in application rejection. Our AI tool produces a correctly exposed, sharp JPEG output that passes automated biometric checks.

The photo must have been taken within the last six months. Italian consulates are noted for being particularly strict on this rule — a photo within the six-month window that no longer reflects the applicant's current appearance (due to changes in hairstyle, colour, or facial hair) may be rejected and a newer photo requested.

name: New Zealand Passport

New Zealand Passport Photo Requirements 2026 — Complete DIA Official Guide

Getting your New Zealand passport photo right in 2026 is more important than ever. The Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) uses advanced automated biometric facial recognition software to verify every photo submitted through the official passports.govt.nz online renewal portal — and even minor errors in background, head size, or expression will trigger an instant rejection. Whether you are renewing your NZ passport online, applying for the first time, or submitting from overseas at a New Zealand embassy or consulate, this complete guide covers every official requirement you need to know.

The standard New Zealand passport photo size for printed applications is 35mm wide × 45mm tall — the same international ICAO biometric format used by Australia, the UK, and most of Europe. For online digital submissions through the DIA passport renewal portal, your JPEG photo must be between 900 × 1200 pixels and 4500 × 6000 pixels, with a file size between 500KB and 10MB. The photo must be in portrait orientation (taller than wide) with a 3:4 aspect ratio. Scanned photos and photos taken with the front-facing selfie camera are not accepted — the DIA requires someone else to take your photo using a rear camera from approximately 1.5 metres away to maintain correct facial proportions and avoid lens distortion.

Background Color — The #1 Reason NZ Passport Photos Get Rejected

The background of your New Zealand passport photo must be plain, light-coloured, and completely uniform — with no patterns, textures, gradients, shadows, or objects visible anywhere in the frame. The DIA accepts white, light gray, cream, or light blue backgrounds, provided there is strong visual contrast between your face and the background. The background must be evenly lit — any shadow cast by your head or body onto the background is grounds for rejection. Stand at least 1–1.5 metres away from the background surface to prevent shadow formation. Do not digitally remove or replace your background using photo editing apps or AI tools — the DIA checker detects artificial backgrounds and flags them as non-compliant.

Head Size, Face Position, and Biometric Framing Requirements

Your head — measured from the bottom of your chin to the top of your hair — must occupy between 70% and 80% of the total photo height. In physical terms for a 35×45mm print, this means your head height must be between 32mm and 36mm. The face must be perfectly centered in the frame, with a clear visible gap between the top of your head and the top edge of the photo. Your full shoulders and upper chest must be included in the lower portion of the frame. The head must be held completely upright — no tilting, turning, or leaning in any direction. Both eyes must be at an equal height and positioned between 55% and 65% from the bottom of the photo frame, which is the standard ICAO biometric eye-line requirement used by the DIA's automated photo checker.

Facial Expression, Eyes, and Mouth Rules

The DIA requires a completely neutral facial expression for all New Zealand passport photos. Your mouth must be firmly closed — no smiling, no open mouth, no visible teeth. Your eyes must be fully open and looking directly into the camera lens. Squinting, half-open eyes, or eyes obscured by hair are all grounds for rejection. Your hair must be tucked away from your face, kept clear of your eyes and eyebrows, and must not cover the edges of your face. The photo must be a true, natural likeness — no filters, AI enhancement, skin smoothing, blemish removal, or any other form of digital retouching is permitted under DIA guidelines.

Glasses, Accessories, and Clothing Policy 2026

Prescription glasses are technically permitted for New Zealand passport photos if the lenses are completely clear and untinted, the frames do not obscure or cover the eyes, and there is zero glare or flash reflection on the lenses. However, the DIA strongly recommends removing glasses for the photo to eliminate any risk of rejection. Sunglasses, tinted glasses, thick-framed glasses, and colored contact lenses are strictly prohibited. Head coverings are not permitted unless worn daily for verified religious or medical reasons — in which case a signed statutory declaration is required with the application, and the complete face from forehead to chin must remain fully visible with no shadows. Clothing should be everyday attire in plain, contrasting colors — avoid white or very light clothing that may blend with a light background.

Children and Infant Passport Photo Rules

Every New Zealand child, including newborns, requires their own separate passport — and their photo must meet the same DIA standards as adults. For infants who cannot sit upright, lay the baby on a plain white or light-colored sheet and photograph from directly above. No parent hands, toys, pacifiers, or car seat structures should be visible in the frame. The baby's face must be fully visible and as close to neutral as possible — partially open eyes are tolerated for very young infants. For toddlers and older children, both eyes must be open, the mouth closed, and the face directed straight at the camera. The same 35×45mm dimensions and 70–80% head coverage rule apply regardless of age.

Background Requirements for NZ Visa Photos

The background must be plain, light-coloured, and completely uniform — white, light gray, or cream are all acceptable, provided there is strong contrast between the background and your face, hair, and clothing. The background must contain no shadows, no patterns, no textures, no objects, and no other people. Stand at least 1–1.5 metres from the background to prevent shadows. Face Size, Head Position, and Biometric Compliance

Your face must occupy 70% to 80% of the total photo height, measured from the bottom of your chin to the top of your head including hair. This is the standard ICAO biometric requirement applied consistently by Immigration New Zealand across all visa categories. The head must be perfectly centered in the frame, held upright with no tilt, rotation, or lean in any direction. Your full shoulders and upper chest must be visible at the bottom of the frame. Both eyes must be positioned between 55% and 65% from the bottom of the image — this eye-line positioning is verified automatically by the INZ digital photo checker. There must be a visible clear gap between the top of your head and the top edge of the photo.

Expression, Eyes, Lighting, and Photo Quality

Immigration New Zealand requires a completely neutral facial expression for all visa photos in 2026. The mouth must be firmly closed with no visible teeth. Your eyes must be fully open, looking directly into the camera. Hair must be tucked away from your face, clear of your eyes and eyebrows, and must not cover the sides of your face or the top of your forehead. The photo must be sharp, in precise focus, and free from motion blur, pixelation, red-eye, overexposure, or underexposure. Lighting must represent your true, natural skin tone — no flash hotspots or dark areas on the face are permitted. The photo must be a true, unmodified representation of your natural appearance — no beauty filters, skin-smoothing effects, blemish removal, or any digital alterations are permitted under INZ photo guidelines.

Prescription glasses are permitted for New Zealand visa photos provided they have completely clear, untinted lenses, zero glare or flash reflections, and do not cover or obstruct the eyes in any way. Head coverings are only permitted for verified religious or medical reasons — the full face including forehead, cheeks, and chin must be completely visible with no shadows cast. Jewelry and facial piercings are acceptable as long as they do not cover or obscure any facial features. Clothing should be plain everyday attire in mid-toned colors — avoid white or very light colors that may blend into a light background.

passportcontent:
Poland Passport Photo: Official Requirements for 2026

According to the guidance published on the gov.pl portal by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Administration (MSWiA), a Polish passport photo must measure 35 × 45 mm. The photo must be current — take it no earlier than 6 months before submitting the application. The face occupies 70–80% of the frame, and the image includes the entire head from the crown plus the upper part of the shoulders. These rules stem directly from the Act of 27 January 2022 on Passport Documents and the Act of 6 August 2010 on Identity Cards, since one photo satisfies both documents. In fact, this standard format matches the exact rozmiar zdjęcia do dowodu (ID card photo size) and serves perfectly as a zdjęcie do prawa jazdy (driving license photo) as well.

Poland Passport Photo — Technical Specifications

Head Position and Facial Expression

Face the camera lens directly — never tilt your head or turn it in a three-quarter angle. The full oval of the face stays visible, and your expression remains natural, with no facial gestures. Keep your mouth closed and your eyebrows uncovered. Your eyes must stay naturally open, clearly visible along with the pupils, and look straight into the lens — a red-eye effect disqualifies the photo. Ears don't need to be visible, and hair may extend beyond the frame's outline. If a medical condition prevents you from meeting these requirements, the office accepts a photo with closed eyes, an open mouth, or an unnatural expression.

Corrective Glasses, Contact Lenses, and Vision Impairments

You may wear corrective glasses in the photo if your eyes remain clearly visible, the frames don't cover your eyebrows, and the lenses show no light reflections. Contact lenses are permitted as long as they don't alter the natural shape or color of your eyes. Applicants with a congenital or acquired vision impairment may wear tinted glasses in the photo — in that case, attach a disability certificate to the application. For an online application, submit the certificate as a signed electronic document or a scan, and hand over the original to the clerk when collecting the document.

Head Coverings, Facial Hair, and Jewelry

Head coverings aren't allowed, except when required by religion — in that case, the face must remain fully visible, along with the complete facial oval and the line of the ears. Attach a certificate confirming membership in a religious community registered in Poland. Facial hair, a beard, or a moustache pose no obstacle as long as they don't hinder identification — for best results, however, consider taking the photo clean-shaven. Jewelry is permitted, provided it doesn't cover the facial oval or disrupt the uniform background.

Background, Lighting, and Technical Quality

The background stays white, evenly lit, free of shadows and decorative elements. Your face must be evenly illuminated — light reflections on the skin or hair and shadows on the face are both unacceptable. Only the applicant may appear in the frame. The photo must be sharp, free of visible pixelation, with natural contrast and a clearly defined head outline. Coloring stays neutral, and tonal density remains balanced — the photo can be neither too bright nor too dark. The image must show no creases or surface damage and must faithfully reproduce your natural skin tone.

Digital vs. Paper Format — Two Application Paths

The required photo format depends on how you submit the application. An online passport application applies only to children under 12 years old — in that case, attach a digital color photo with a minimum resolution of 768 × 1004 pixels and a file size up to 2.5 MB, keeping proportions equivalent to the 35 × 45 mm format. All other applicants submit the application in person at the office and bring a color photo printed on photographic paper in the 35 × 45 mm format — the office won't accept a digital file in this case. The same rules apply to the identity card: an online application requires a digital photo with a minimum resolution of 492 × 633 pixels, while an in-person application requires a paper print with the same proportions.

Photos of Children Under 5

Children under five years old may have closed eyes, an open mouth, or an unnatural expression in the photo. The child's face stays uncovered — not obscured by hair or a toy — and the child holds their head straight. The background must be light and uniform, with no other people in the frame.

Where to Submit Your Passport Application

You submit a passport application in person at any Voivodeship Office (Urząd Wojewódzki), its branch, or a Polish consulate abroad. The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Administration is the institution responsible for the requirements and the procedure. Detailed photo instructions are published by the gov.pl portal as an official PDF document, available for download on the office's website.

Photo Compliance Checklist

  • Size: 35 × 45 mm, color photo.
  • Background: white, uniform, free of shadows and decoration.
  • Face: occupies 70–80% of the frame, fully visible from the crown to the upper shoulders.
  • Expression: natural, mouth closed, eyes open and facing the lens.
  • Head coverings: not allowed except for documented religious reasons.
  • Glasses: permitted without tinted lenses and without light reflections.
  • Recency: photo taken no more than 6 months before submission.
  • Format: paper print for in-person applications; digital only for online applications by children under 12.

Avoid Passport Application Rejection in 2026

A non-compliant photo is one of the most common reasons applications get rejected at the Voivodeship Office. Our AI tool checks head framing, face coverage percentage, background uniformity, and eye position against MSWiA guidelines — and produces a ready 35 × 45 mm photo for immediate submission at the office or consulate.

The requirements come from the consular sections of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (msz.gov.pl) and rest on Article 10 of the Community Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009). The photo must be sharp, clean, and well-contrasted, printed on high-quality paper against a white background, no older than 6 months, and clear enough to identify the applicant.

Head Position and Facial Expression

The photo shows the applicant without a head covering, looking straight into the lens, with the mouth closed. Hair must not cover the face, and the frame clearly shows the eyes and the full face from both sides — from the crown of the head to the upper shoulders. This specification comes directly from Article 10 of the Community Visa Code and applies uniformly across every Polish consular post, regardless of the country where you submit the application.

Corrective Glasses

If you wear glasses, the photo must meet additional criteria: the lenses stay untinted, the frame doesn't cover any part of the eye, and no light reflections appear on the lenses. If your travel document shows a photo of you wearing glasses, attach a photo taken with glasses to the visa application as well — the consulate checks that your appearance matches your passport.

Biometric Data and Fingerprint Collection

Under Article 13 of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, when you submit a visa application at a consular office or a Visa Application Centre, the officer collects biometric data from you, including a facial photograph and ten fingerprints. The photo attached to the application forms the basis for this verification, so it must accurately reflect your current appearance.

Visa Types and Rules That Apply Uniformly

A Schengen Type C visa allows a stay in the Schengen area of up to 90 days within any 180-day period, and it covers either every Schengen state or, in its limited-territorial-validity version, selected member states. A National Type D visa lets you stay in Poland for up to one year while also allowing travel within the Schengen area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Photo requirements stay identical for both visa types — the differences concern only the supporting documents proving the purpose of travel and the consular fee.

Travel Document and Other Attachments

Attach a valid travel document to your visa application that meets specific criteria: validity for at least three months beyond the planned departure from the Schengen area, at least two blank pages reserved for visas, and issuance within the last ten years. You also need travel health insurance valid across the entire Schengen area, covering your planned stay, with a minimum coverage of EUR 30,000.

Registering Your Application Through e-konsulat

You register your visa application electronically through e-konsulat.gov.pl, where you select the relevant consular post and book an appointment. The consul responsible for reviewing the application is always the consul of the Schengen state that represents the main destination of the trip. You can't send documents by fax, regular mail, or email — you submit the complete application in person at the scheduled appointment at the consulate.

  • Glasses: untinted lenses, no light reflections, frame doesn't cover the eye.
  • Recency: photo taken no more than 6 months before submission.
  • Copies: one photo glued to the application form.
  • Legal basis: Article 10 of the Community Visa Code (EC No 810/2009).

The South Korean passport, officially issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, is one of the world's most powerful travel documents — granting visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to over 190 countries as of 2026. To maintain this status, the Korean government enforces some of the strictest biometric photo standards in the world, fully aligned with the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) guidelines. Understanding and meeting these requirements in 2026 is essential to avoid application delays or outright rejection at consulate offices worldwide.

The required photo size is 35mm wide × 45mm tall (approximately 1.38 × 1.77 inches). The digital equivalent must be 413 × 531 pixels at 300 DPI — the standard for all Korean consulate and Ministry of Foreign Affairs submissions. The photo must be printed in full color on high-quality photo paper; matte or glossy finishes are both acceptable. Only one printed photo is required when applying in person at a Korean consulate abroad. Digital photos are not accepted for passport applications — a physical print is mandatory.

Head Size and Facial Geometry Standards

The head must measure between 32mm and 36mm from the crown (excluding hair) to the chin, which translates to 70% to 80% of the total photo height. The face must be perfectly centered and front-facing, with both ears fully visible — a requirement that surprises many first-time applicants. Hair must not cover the forehead, eyebrows, or ears. The eyes must be open, looking directly into the camera, and must not be obstructed by hair, glasses, or any accessory.

Background, Lighting, and Expression Rules

The background must be pure white (#FFFFFF) with no gradients, shadows, patterns, or other people or objects. Lighting must be uniform — no flash reflections on the face or background, and absolutely no red-eye. The expression must be completely neutral: mouth firmly closed, no smiling, no frowning. This is not a stylistic preference — Korean facial recognition software at Incheon Airport's automated immigration gates uses precise biometric mapping of the distance between facial landmarks. Any expression that alters the mouth contour, raises the cheeks, or shifts the nose-to-chin distance can cause biometric mismatch and immigration delays.

Clothing, Accessories, and Prohibited Items (2026 Update)

Applicants must not wear white clothing, as it cannot be distinguished from the white background. Uniforms of any kind are prohibited. Glasses are strongly discouraged in 2026 — updated Korean consulate guidelines now explicitly recommend removing eyeglasses due to the high rejection rate caused by glare, frame obstruction, or lens distortion. Tinted glasses, sunglasses, and colored contact lenses are strictly forbidden. Head coverings are not permitted unless required for religious or verified medical reasons, and even then, the full face from forehead to chin must remain fully visible.

Recency and Authenticity Requirements

The photo must have been taken within the last six months prior to the date of application. Digital retouching, beauty filters, skin smoothing, Photoshop editing, or any form of AI-generated alteration of the applicant's appearance is strictly prohibited. The photo must be a true, unmodified representation of the applicant's natural appearance — including skin tone, facial features, and any natural marks.

Official Swedish Passport Photo Size and Dimensions

Background Colour: Why Pure White Matters

The background of your Swedish passport photo must be plain white — not off-white, not light grey, not cream. That works out to roughly 32–36 mm of face height within the frame. If your head is too small — a very common result of standing too far from the camera — the photo will be rejected. Eye Height Positioning in a Swedish Passport Photo

Face Size, Positioning, and Head Alignment

The face — measured from the top of the head including hair, to the bottom of the chin — must occupy between 70% and 80% of the photo's total height. The head must be centered within the frame, positioned straight on with no tilting or rotation to either side. Both edges of the face must be clearly visible, and both eyes must be open, level, and directed straight at the camera. Hair must not drape over or obscure the eyes or forehead. The photo must show the head and partial shoulders — it is a close-up portrait, not a full-body image.

Background and Lighting Requirements

The background must be plain white or off-white with no patterns, textures, gradients, or objects. Any shadows falling on the background or across the face will cause the photo to be rejected. Even and balanced lighting across the face is essential — overexposed photos (where facial features are washed out) and underexposed photos (where features appear too dark) are both unacceptable. Standing approximately one meter away from the background wall when the photo is taken helps prevent shadow problems.

Glasses, Headwear, and Appearance Rules

Glasses may officially be worn in Thai passport photos, but the Department of Consular Affairs strongly advises their removal to eliminate the risk of rejection caused by glare, thick frames obscuring facial features, or tinted lenses. If glasses are kept on, there must be zero glare on the lenses, the frames must be thin, and no tint is permitted. Sunglasses are never allowed. Hats and headwear are prohibited except for religious or medical head coverings — in those cases, the face must remain completely unobstructed from chin to forehead. Earphones, headsets, and similar accessories are not permitted. Uniforms should not be worn.

Color, Format, and Print Quality

The photo must be in color — black and white photographs are not accepted for Thai passport applications. The print must be of continuous-tone photographic quality. Ordinary inkjet printer printouts are not appropriate for consular submission. The image must be sharp, in focus, and free of pixelation, blur, red-eye, or any visible digital manipulation. Brightness and contrast must accurately represent the applicant's natural appearance.

Children, Infants, and Applicants Under 20

Passport regulations apply to Thai nationals of all ages, including newborns, who each require their own individual passport and a separate photo taken within the last six months. For infants, toys, bottles, pacifiers, and other objects must not appear in the photo. If a parent must hold the infant, hands and arms may not be visible in the frame. Placing the infant on a white cloth on a flat surface is a practical approach to achieve the required white background. Applicants under 20 years of age must be accompanied by both parents when applying at a Thai Embassy or Consulate; they are not eligible to apply online independently.

Important: Passport Production and Delivery

All Thai e-passports are produced centrally by the Department of Consular Affairs in Bangkok and distributed by airmail to embassies and consulates worldwide. Thai nationals aged 20 and over may apply for passport renewal online through their nearest Thai Embassy, receiving the completed passport by mail. Online renewal is not available for applicants under 20 years old.

The background must be plain white or off-white with absolutely no patterns, shadows, furniture, or objects visible. Shadows across the face or on the background behind the head are a primary reason for photo rejection by Thai consular officers. To avoid background shadows, stand or sit at least 50 cm away from the wall when the photo is taken, and use soft, even lighting. Overexposed images — where the background bleeds into the face — and underexposed images — where facial features are obscured — are both rejected. Glasses are officially permitted in Thai visa photos provided the frames do not obstruct the eyes, there is no glare on the lenses, and the lenses are not tinted. The photo must have been taken within the last six months. Using an older photo — even one that is otherwise technically correct — is a grounds for rejection, particularly on renewal applications where the officer can compare against the previous visa photo. Selfies are not acceptable for Thai visa applications. The only official website for Thai visa applications is thaievisa.go.th, operated by the Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Thailand.   • Wear clothing that contrasts with a white or light grey background; skip white tops and uniforms
  • Skip head coverings unless worn for documented religious reasons, keeping your forehead-to-chin fully visible
  • Use a photo taken within 6 months of your application date

One Tool, Every Portugal Visa Category

Type C Schengen tourist and business visas, Type D national long-stay visas, the D7 passive income visa, the D8 digital nomad visa, the D2 entrepreneur visa, and the Golden Visa (ARI) all share the identical 35×45mm, 70%–80% head-coverage standard. Registering with AIMA for a residence permit after arrival uses the same format too, so one export from this tool covers your consulate application and your later AIMA biometric appointment without adjusting a single setting.

Digital File Plus a Print-Ready Sheet

A successful digital upload does not end the requirement — most VFS Global and consulate appointments still need two identical printed photos on high-quality photo paper, free of creases or marks. Every download from this tool pairs the portal-ready digital file with a print-ready A4 sheet, built from the same source image.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the same photo work for my Schengen visa and my later AIMA residence permit?

Yes. Both use the identical 35×45mm size and 70%–80% head-coverage standard, so one export from this tool covers your consulate application now and your AIMA biometric appointment later.

Why does my upload get rejected even though it looks fine on screen?

The usual invisible causes are a file over the typical 500KB portal limit, a background reading as off-white under automated review, or a head-height ratio just outside 32mm–36mm. This tool checks and corrects all three before export.

Can I wear my glasses in a Portugal visa photo?

Thin prescription frames with zero glare are technically allowed, but removing them entirely is the recommended path since any reflection or tint triggers a rejection at VFS pre-check.

Do I need a different photo for a family member applying with me?

Yes. Every applicant, including children, needs an individual photo with no other person in frame — run each family member's photo through the tool separately.

Can I use my Portugal passport photo for my visa application too?

The 35×45mm size matches, but glasses and background rules differ slightly between the two documents, so re-upload your source photo here to get a visa-specific export.

Portugal Visa Approved — Schengen, D7, D8 and Golden Visa Ready

From short-stay Schengen applications at your local Portuguese consulate to D7, D8, and Golden Visa submissions at VFS Global and AIMA, this AI photo tool builds a fully compliant 35×45mm Portugal visa photo — correct background colour, biometric head sizing, and no retouching — ready for 2026 submissions.

Türk Pasaportu Biyometrik Fotoğraf Gereksinimleri 2026

Türkiye Cumhuriyeti biyometrik pasaportu için fotoğraf standartları, T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı ve Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü tarafından belirlenmektedir. 2026 yılı itibarıyla bu standartlar, yurt içinde nüfus müdürlüklerine yapılan başvurularda ve yurt dışındaki Türk konsolosluklarında aynı şekilde uygulanmaktadır. Pasaport başvurunuzun ilk seferde onaylanması için fotoğrafınızın aşağıdaki zorunlu teknik özellikleri tam olarak karşılaması gerekmektedir.

Resmi Boyut ve Format Gereksinimleri

Türk biyometrik pasaportu için kabul edilen tek fotoğraf boyutu 50 mm × 60 mm'dir. Bu boyut, birçok ülkede kullanılan standart 35×45 mm pasaport fotoğrafından belirgin biçimde farklıdır; bu nedenle genel amaçlı pasaport fotoğraf hizmetlerine başvurmak ret riskini artırır. T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı Konsolosluğu'nun 4 Eylül 2024 tarihli resmi bildirisine göre, ABD'de 2×2 inç (yaklaşık 51×51 mm) boyutundaki fotoğraflar istisna olarak kabul edilmektedir; ancak Türkiye'de yapılacak başvurularda yalnızca 50×60 mm geçerlidir. Fotoğrafın dijital çözünürlüğü baskı kalitesini doğrudan etkiler; 300 DPI baskıda 590×709 piksel karşılık gelir. Dosya formatı JPEG olmalıdır.

T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı'nın resmi kılavuzuna göre fotoğraf arka planının düz beyaz ve desensiz olması zorunludur. Gri veya krem rengi arka planlar kabul edilmez. Işıklandırma, yüzün tamamının açıkça görülebilecek şekilde yeterli parlaklıkta olmasını sağlamalı; aynı zamanda aşırı parlaklık, gölge veya yansımadan kaçınılmalıdır. Arka plan üzerinde ya da yüz üzerinde oluşan gölgeler fotoğrafın reddedilmesine neden olur. Keskinlik ve kontrast ayarlarının doğru yapılması, yüzün bulanık görünmemesi için kritik öneme sahiptir; odak tamamen yüz üzerinde olmalıdır.

Yüz Konumu ve Poz Gereksinimleri

Fotoğrafta yüzün fotoğraf yüksekliğinin yüzde yetmişi ile seksenini kaplaması gerekmektedir. Başın öne eğilmemesi ya da yana dönmemesi; kameraya dik, tam cepheden bakılması zorunludur. Gözler tamamen açık olmalı ve doğrudan kameraya bakmalıdır. İfade nötr olmalı, dudaklar kapalı tutulmalıdır; gülümseme kabul edilmez. Saçlar yüzü kapatmamalı, kulaklar mümkünse görünür olmalıdır. Fotoğraf, yüksek kaliteli bir kamerayla çekilmeli ve kaliteli fotoğraf kağıdına basılmalıdır; yırtık, buruşuk ya da ezik fotoğraflar kesinlikle kabul edilmez.

Aksesuar ve Kıyafet Kuralları

Resmi kılavuz, gözlük, küpe, şapka ve başlık gibi aksesuarların kullanımını açıkça yasaklamaktadır; bunlar yüzün görünürlüğünü engelleyen her türlü kıyafet ve aksesuar ile birlikte reddedilir. Yalnızca belgelenmiş tıbbi gereklilik durumunda gözlük takılabilir. Dini amaçlı başörtüsü veya baş örtüsü kabul edilir; ancak bu durumda uygulamanın dini niteliğini doğrulayan imzalı bir beyan sunulması gerekir ve yüzün hiçbir bölümü örtülmemelidir. Tıbbi nedenle baş örtüsü kullanılıyorsa imzalı bir doktor beyanı eklenmelidir.

Fotoğraf Tazeliği

Fotoğrafın başvuru tarihinden en fazla altı ay önce çekilmiş olması ve başvuru sahibinin güncel görünümünü yansıtması gerekmektedir. Saç rengi, yüz şekli veya diğer belirgin özelliklerde önemli değişiklikler olması durumunda yeni bir fotoğraf çekilmesi zorunludur.

Çocuklar ve Bebekler İçin Fotoğraf Kuralları

Resmi kılavuza göre yukarıdaki tüm kurallar çocuklar ve bebekler için de geçerlidir. Fotoğrafta yalnızca başvurulan çocuk yer almalıdır; ebeveyn ya da başka bir kişi görünmemelidir. Bebek koltuğu, oyuncak veya benzeri ekipman fotoğrafta bulunmamalıdır. Başını tutamayan bebek ve küçük çocuklar için düz beyaz ya da kırık beyaz bir bez veya yüzey üzerine sırt üstü yatırılarak fotoğraf çekilebilir.

Nüfus Müdürlüğü İçin Onaylı Pasaport Fotoğrafı

Türk pasaportu başvurusunda fotoğraf nedeniyle ret yaşamamak için boyut, arka plan, ifade ve aksesuar kurallarına eksiksiz uymak gerekir. Yapay zeka destekli aracımız, T.C. Dışişleri Bakanlığı'nın 4 Eylül 2024 tarihli resmi biyometrik fotoğraf kılavuzuna uygun olarak yüzü 50×60 mm'lik alana otomatik olarak hizalar, arka planı saf beyaza dönüştürür ve JPEG formatında 300 DPI çözünürlükte teslim eder. Tek seferde, garantili sonuç.

UK Biometric Passport: Official HMPO Photo Requirements 2026

His Majesty's Passport Office (HMPO) sets the photo standards for all British passport applications — whether you are applying for the first time, renewing, or adding pages. The physical print size is 35 × 45 mm (width × height), the standard used in all UK photo booths. For online applications through GOV.UK, a digital file is required instead: minimum 600 × 750 pixels, between 50 KB and 10 MB, in JPEG format. HMPO updated its Photo Standards to Version 49.0 on 8 December 2025, and those rules are fully in force for all 2026 applications.

UK Passport — Official HMPO Specifications

Print Size
35 × 45 mm
Head Height
29–34 mm
Background
Cream / Light Grey
Digital Min
600 × 750 px

50 KB – 10 MB

≤ 1 Month

Format

The One-Month Recency Rule — UK's Strictest Requirement

The single most important rule that separates UK passport photos from those of almost every other country: your photo must have been taken within the last month before you submit your application. This applies to all applicants — adults, children, and infants — for both new applications and renewals. GOV.UK states this explicitly: a photo taken more than one month before submission will cause your application to be delayed. This is considerably stricter than the six-month window used by most other countries, and HMPO's December 2025 update tightened enforcement of this rule further. Do not take your photo weeks in advance while gathering other documents — photograph yourself as close to your submission date as possible.

Background: Cream or Light Grey — Not White

GOV.UK's printed photo guidance specifies the background must be plain cream or light grey. For digital uploads, the requirement is a plain light-coloured background. This is one of the most frequently misunderstood rules: applicants used to the pure white background required by the US and most Schengen countries often use a white wall and get flagged by HMPO's automated checker. The GOV.UK digital submission system uses automated photo-checking technology that is particularly sensitive to background contrast. A plain light grey background produces the most consistent pass rate with HMPO's automated system. The background must be completely plain — no patterns, no gradients, no visible furniture, and no shadows behind you.

Head Size: 29–34 mm Chin to Crown

The image of your face — measured from the bottom of your chin to the top of your head (crown) — must be between 29 mm and 34 mm within the 45 mm tall frame. This translates to approximately 65–75% of the photo height. This range is tighter than most applicants expect. HMPO figures show that around one in five online applications is affected by a photo problem, and incorrect head sizing is among the most common causes of rejection. Your eyes must be open and clearly visible, and your hair must not fall in front of your eyes.

Glasses: Avoid Unless Medically Necessary

GOV.UK's current guidance states clearly: do not wear glasses in your photo unless you have to do so. If you must wear glasses for a documented medical reason, they cannot be sunglasses or tinted glasses, and your eyes must not be covered by the frames or obscured by any glare, reflection, or shadow. HMPO strongly recommends removing glasses to prevent automatic rejection by its photo-checking system. Head coverings are not allowed except for religious or medical reasons, and even then, your full face must remain visible from chin to forehead.

Expression, Pose, and Clothing

Per GOV.UK, your photo must show a plain expression with your mouth closed. Both eyes must be open and looking directly at the camera. You must face forwards — no tilting or turning. Your full head and upper shoulders must be visible, and the photo must contain no other people or objects. There are no restrictions on everyday clothing, but clothing must be in clear contrast to the background. Uniforms are not prohibited by HMPO's photo rules, though the general guidance is to wear normal attire.

Paper vs. Online Applications in 2026

Paper applications require 2 identical printed photos submitted loose with your form. Online applications through GOV.UK require a single digital upload, or you can enter a photo code obtained from a photo booth or shop (such as Timpson, Snappy Snaps, or Max Spielmann) — these services transmit the photo directly to HMPO. The online application fee is £94.50; the paper form costs £107, following the April 2025 fee increase. Photos taken with your own device are accepted for online applications but are described by GOV.UK as less likely to be approved than photos from a booth or shop.

Compliance Checklist — HMPO Photo Standards v49.0 (December 2025)

  • Size: 35 × 45 mm printed; 600–900 × 750–1125 px digital.
  • Background: Plain cream or light grey (printed); plain light-coloured (digital). No pure white, no patterns, no shadows.
  • Head Height: 29–34 mm chin to crown within the frame.
  • Recency: Taken within the last month — not 6 months.
  • Expression: Plain/neutral, mouth closed, eyes open, looking straight at the camera.
  • Hair: Must not cover eyes or face.
  • Glasses: Remove unless medically required. No tinted lenses, no glare.
  • Head Coverings: Only for religious or medical reasons; full face must remain visible.
  • No shadows on face or background.
  • No digital alterations — unaltered colour photo on plain white photographic paper (for print).
  • Printed copies: 2 identical, separated and loose (paper applications).

One in Five Applications Delayed by Photo Problems

HMPO data shows approximately one in five online passport applications encounters a photo issue. The most common causes are an incorrect background colour (white instead of cream or light grey), head size outside the 29–34 mm range, and photos taken more than one month before submission. Our AI tool validates all three against the HMPO Photo Standards v49.0 before you upload, producing a GOV.UK-ready file that meets every technical requirement for a 2026 British passport application.

Background Colour: Cream or Light Grey

The UK visa photo background must be plain cream or light grey — the same standard applied to HMPO passport photos. A pure white background, which is required for US, Schengen, and many other visa applications, is not the preferred background for UK documents. This distinction catches many applicants off guard. The background must be completely plain with no patterns, objects, or shadows. Any shadow behind you — even a faint one — is grounds for rejection. The photo must also show a clear contrast between your face and the background, which is why a plain light grey works reliably across all skin tones.

The One-Month Rule Applies to Visas Too

Just as with UK passport photos, your visa photo must have been taken within the last month before you submit your application. This is one of the strictest recency requirements of any major immigration authority globally. Do not reuse a photo taken for another purpose, even a recent one — if it was taken more than four weeks before your visa submission date, it will not be compliant. Two identical copies must be submitted with paper-based visa applications.

Face, Expression, and Head Positioning

Your face must be centred in the frame and take up 65–75% of the photo height — corresponding to a chin-to-crown measurement of 29–34 mm within the 45 mm frame. You must face directly forward, with both eyes open, clearly visible, and looking straight at the camera. Your expression must be plain and neutral, with your mouth closed. Hair must not fall in front of your eyes. The full head and upper shoulders must be visible — the photo is not just of the face.

Glasses, Head Coverings, and Special Cases

UK visa guidance mirrors HMPO passport rules: do not wear glasses unless you have a documented medical necessity. If glasses must be worn, the lenses must not be tinted, the frames must not cover the eyes, and there must be no glare or reflection. Head coverings are not permitted except for religious or medical reasons, and even then, the complete face from chin to top of forehead — and both sides from ear to ear — must be fully visible. Babies and young children follow relaxed rules: under-ones do not need to have their eyes open, and a supporting hand may be used provided it is not visible in the photo.

Photo Quality and Printing Standards

Visa photos must be printed to a professional standard on plain photographic paper, in colour, and in clear focus. The photo must not be creased, torn, or marked. No computer software alterations are permitted — this includes the removal of blemishes, the adjustment of skin tone, or any other post-processing that changes your natural appearance. The photo must not have red-eye. Both copies submitted must be identical.

Uniform Standard Across All UK Visa Categories

UKVI applies the same 35 × 45 mm photo specification to all visa categories — Standard Visitor, Student, Skilled Worker, Family, and all other routes. There is no variation in photo requirements based on the type of visa you are applying for. The only differences lie in the number of supporting documents and the fee structure. For the most current official requirements, UKVI guidance is published at gov.uk/uk-visa-photo-requirements.

  • Background: Plain cream or light grey. No pure white, no shadows, no patterns.
  • Head Height: 29–34 mm chin to crown (65–75% of frame).
  • Recency: Taken within the last month before submission.
  • Expression: Plain/neutral, mouth closed, eyes open, facing forward.
  • Hair: Must not cover eyes or any part of the face.
  • Glasses: Avoid unless medically required; no tinted lenses, no glare.
  • Head Covering: Only religious or medical exemptions; full face must be visible.
  • Copies: 2 identical prints, unattached and loose.
  • No alterations: Unretouched, no filters, no digital enhancements.

Planning to apply for or renew a Nepal passport in 2026? Getting your passport photo right the first time saves you from costly delays at the Department of Passports office in Tripureshwor, Kathmandu. This complete guide covers every official requirement you need to know — from photo dimensions and background color to facial expression and print quality.

Photo Size and Dimensions

The official Nepal passport photo size is 35 mm × 45 mm (3.5 cm × 4.5 cm), equivalent to approximately 1.37 × 1.77 inches. At a resolution of 600 DPI (dots per inch), this translates to 413 × 531 pixels. Photos that do not meet these exact dimensions will be rejected at the time of application. You are typically required to submit four (4) identical copies of the photo with your application.

Background Requirements

Your Nepal passport photo must have a plain white or very light grey background with no patterns, textures, shadows, or gradient effects. The background must be uniform throughout the entire image. Any shadows falling on the background from the subject will result in automatic rejection. Make sure the background is well-lit and clearly distinguishable from your face and hair.

Head Size and Positioning

The head — measured from the top of the hair to the bottom of the chin — must occupy between 70% and 80% of the total image height. Your face must be centered within the frame, looking directly at the camera. The head must not be tilted, turned, or rotated in any direction. Both ears should ideally be visible. The top of the shoulders should also be included at the bottom of the frame to provide proper context and proportions.

Facial Expression and Eyes

Maintain a neutral facial expression with your mouth closed. Smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, or any exaggerated expression is not allowed. Both eyes must be fully open, clearly visible, and looking directly at the camera. Your eyes should be positioned within the upper half of the photo, roughly between 50% and 65% of the image height from the bottom. Blinking or partially closed eyes are grounds for rejection.

Photo Quality and Technical Standards

The photo must be in full color — black-and-white photos are not accepted. The image must be sharp, in focus, and free from pixelation or blurring. There must be no digital alterations, retouching, filters, or color corrections applied. Lighting must be even across the face with no harsh shadows, hot spots, or glare. The print must be on high-quality photo paper — glossy or matte — and the colors must be true to life. For digital submissions, the file format should be JPEG, and the file size should ideally remain under 300 KB.

Clothing and Accessories

Wear your everyday clothing for the photo. Uniforms, costumes, or clothing that resembles any official or military attire is strictly prohibited. Hats and head coverings are generally not allowed, with the only exceptions being those worn for documented religious or medical reasons — in which case a signed statement from a religious authority or a doctor must accompany the application. Eyeglasses may only be worn if required for medical purposes (with documentation); otherwise, they must be removed. Sunglasses are never permitted under any circumstances. Jewelry and small facial accessories are allowed as long as they do not obscure or cast shadows on any part of your face.

Photo Recency

Nepal passport photos must be taken within the last six months of the application date. Photos that are older than six months are considered outdated and will not be accepted. This ensures that the photo accurately reflects the applicant's current appearance.

ePassport vs. MRP Applications

As of 2026, Nepal's Department of Passports has largely transitioned to issuing ePassports (biometric passports) at the central office in Kathmandu. Some District Administration Offices (DAOs) in remote regions may still process Machine Readable Passport (MRP) applications. The photo requirements are identical for both document types: 35 × 45 mm on a white background at high resolution.

Common Reasons for Rejection

The most frequent reasons Nepal passport photos are rejected include: shadows on the background or face, incorrect head size proportions, photo older than six months, background color that is not plain white or light grey, digital enhancements or retouching, poor print quality from low-resolution studio prints, and wearing non-permitted accessories such as sunglasses or hats.

Tips for a Perfect Nepal Passport Photo

Use even, diffused natural lighting or a professional studio setup. Position yourself approximately one metre from the camera. Have someone else take the photo — selfies are not acceptable for official passport applications. Use a tripod for the camera to avoid motion blur. Always verify your photo against the official dimensions and head-size ratios before submitting your application at the Department of Passports.

Nepal Visa Photo Requirements (2026)

Whether you are applying for a Nepal tourist visa, a Nepal visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA), or submitting an advance application through the official Department of Immigration portal, your visa photo must meet strict official specifications. A non-compliant photo is one of the leading causes of visa application delays and rejections. This comprehensive guide covers every official Nepal visa photo requirement for 2026.

Photo Size and Dimensions

The Nepal visa photo must measure exactly 35 mm × 45 mm (3.5 × 4.5 cm), the same standard size as the Nepal passport photo. This is equivalent to approximately 1.37 × 1.77 inches. Photos submitted for visa on arrival at TIA or via the online immigration portal must conform to these precise dimensions. Incorrect sizing will trigger rejection at the immigration counter or during the online form validation process.

Background Color

The background must be a plain white or very light grey color — uniform, smooth, and completely free of patterns, textures, gradients, or any other distractions. No objects, furniture, or other people should be visible in the background. Shadows cast on the background by the applicant are not acceptable and will lead to the photo being refused. The background should be evenly lit to ensure a clean, professional appearance throughout the entire image.

Head Size and Facial Framing

The head must be centered within the frame and occupy 70% to 80% of the total image height, measured from the crown of the head to the bottom of the chin. The face must be positioned straight and looking directly into the camera. The top of the shoulders must be visible at the lower portion of the frame. Neither the face nor the head should be cut off at any edge of the photograph. Both ears should ideally be visible in the photo.

Facial Expression and Eye Position

A neutral, relaxed facial expression is required — mouth closed, no smiling, no frowning, and no raised eyebrows. Both eyes must be wide open and clearly visible, looking directly at the lens. The eyes should be positioned in the upper half of the image. Ensure there are no reflections or glare on spectacle lenses. Squinting or partially closed eyes will result in the photo being declined.

Photo Quality and Technical Specifications

The Nepal visa photo must be in full color. The image must be sharp, properly focused, and free of blur, noise, or pixelation. No digital editing, retouching, beauty filters, or artificial enhancements are permitted. Lighting must be even across the face — avoid harsh direct flash that creates hot spots or deep shadows around the nose and chin. For digital/online submissions, the photo file format must be JPEG with a minimum resolution of 300 DPI and a maximum file size of 5 MB. For printed physical submissions, use high-quality glossy or matte photo paper to ensure accurate color reproduction and sharpness.

Clothing and Accessories

Wear your regular, everyday clothes that contrast clearly with the white or light grey background. Avoid clothing that is entirely white or very light, as it may blend into the background and create compliance issues. Hats, caps, and head coverings are not permitted, unless worn for verified religious or medical reasons — in both cases, appropriate documentation must be provided, and the full face must remain clearly visible with no shadows. Sunglasses are strictly prohibited. Regular prescription eyeglasses are generally discouraged; if worn, they must not produce glare or obscure the eyes in any way. Accessories such as small jewelry are acceptable provided they do not cast shadows on the face or obstruct facial features.

Children and Infants

Children applying for Nepal visas must have individual photos that meet the same specifications as adults. The photo must show only the child — no hands, toys, or supporting adults should be visible. For infants, closed eyes may be acceptable given the difficulty of keeping very young children still, but open eyes are always preferred. The child's head must be straight and fully visible, with the face centered within the frame.

Photo Recency

Visa photos must have been taken within the past six months of the date of application. This requirement applies to both online applications through the Department of Immigration portal and physical applications submitted at Nepalese embassies or consulates abroad, as well as visa-on-arrival applications at TIA.

Visa on Arrival — Photo Tips

For travelers applying for a Nepal visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, having your compliant photo prepared in advance is strongly recommended, particularly during peak tourist seasons (spring and autumn) when queues at the immigration kiosks can be long. The kiosk machines at TIA also accept digital photo uploads when completing the arrival form online in advance via the Department of Immigration's official website.

Common Reasons for Nepal Visa Photo Rejection

Frequent rejection reasons include: photo older than six months, incorrect dimensions, colored or patterned background, shadows on the face or background, excessive digital retouching, file size exceeding 5 MB for online submissions, non-JPEG file formats, sunglasses or non-permitted head coverings, and poor print quality on the physical copy.

Summary Checklist

Before submitting your Nepal visa application, verify: ✔ Size is 35 × 45 mm ✔ Background is plain white or very light grey ✔ Head occupies 70–80% of image height ✔ Face is centered, straight, and looking at the camera ✔ Both eyes are open and visible ✔ Neutral expression, mouth closed ✔ No sunglasses or non-religious head coverings ✔ Full color, no retouching or filters ✔ Photo taken within the last 6 months ✔ JPEG format, minimum 300 DPI, under 5 MB for online submission

Sri Lanka Passport Photo Requirements (2026)

Submitting the correct passport photo is one of the most critical steps in your Sri Lanka passport application. The Department of Immigration and Emigration of Sri Lanka enforces strict biometric photo standards, and any non-compliant photo will result in your application being rejected or delayed. This complete guide outlines every official requirement you need to meet for a Sri Lanka passport photo in 2026 — from dimensions and background to facial expression and print quality.

Photo Size and Dimensions

The official Sri Lanka passport photo size is 35 mm × 45 mm (3.5 cm × 4.5 cm), equivalent to approximately 1.37 × 1.77 inches. At 600 DPI resolution, this corresponds to 413 × 531 pixels. Photos that deviate from these exact dimensions will not be accepted. Applicants are typically required to submit two to three identical photos along with their application. The photo must be printed on professional-grade continuous-tone photo paper — Polaroid prints and photos produced on standard desktop inkjet or laser printers are explicitly not acceptable.

Background Requirements

According to official specifications published by Sri Lankan embassies, the background must be plain and light-colored — white, light blue, or light grey — and must clearly contrast with the applicant's face and clothing. The background must be entirely free of patterns, textures, gradients, furniture, or any other objects. Uniform lighting must be used to eliminate shadows on the background. Any shadow falling behind the subject will result in the photo being rejected.

Head Size, Position, and Framing

The photo must show a close-up of the head and partial shoulders. The face — measured from the forehead edge to the bottom of the chin — must occupy 70% to 80% of the total photo height, which corresponds to approximately 2.5 cm (25 mm) of the 45 mm image height. The head must be perfectly centered within the frame and positioned straight — no tilting, turning, or angling in any direction. The full face from chin to crown must be visible, and no part of the head should be cut off at any edge.

Eyes, Face, and Expression

Both eyes must be fully open, clearly visible, and looking directly into the camera. No hair should obscure the face, forehead, or ears. The eyes must not be affected by red-eye — photos with red-eye will not be accepted. A neutral facial expression with a closed mouth is required; smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, squinting, or any exaggerated expression is prohibited. The face must be in sharp focus and free from any ink marks, creases, lines, or blemishes on the print.

Lighting and Skin Tone

The photo must have adequate, uniform brightness and contrast. The applicant's skin tone must appear natural — over-exposed photos where skin appears too light, and under-exposed photos where skin appears too dark, will not be accepted. Use diffused, even lighting from the front to avoid harsh shadows on the face, particularly around the nose, chin, and eye sockets. Flash photography should be handled carefully to prevent uneven lighting or glare.

Clothing and Accessories

Wear your everyday, regular clothing for the photo. There is no specific dress code, but clothing should clearly contrast with the background — avoid wearing all-white or very light-colored tops that may blend into the background. Uniforms or costumes that resemble official, military, or government attire are not permitted. Spectacles (glasses) are not accepted under any circumstances for Sri Lanka passport photos — this is an absolute rule stated in the official specifications, with no medical exceptions. Head coverings and head-dress are generally not allowed; however, religious or medical exceptions may apply provided the full face remains clearly visible from chin to forehead with no shadows cast on the face.

Digital Photo Submission Process

For in-country passport applications, the Department of Immigration and Emigration requires applicants to visit an authorized photo studio that is registered with the department's digital photo submission system. The studio captures your biometric photograph and transmits it electronically to the Department's computer system. The studio then issues a Studio Acknowledgement Note, which must be submitted with your application documents. No physical printed photographs are required for in-country applications processed at the Head Office or regional offices. Applicants applying through Sri Lankan Diplomatic Missions overseas may submit applications without a digital photograph, providing fingerprints upon their first arrival in Sri Lanka.

Photo Recency

Passport photos must have been taken within the last six months of your application date. Only current, recent photos that accurately represent your present appearance will be accepted. Photos that are older than six months will be rejected regardless of quality.

Children and Infants

All children, including newborns, must have their own individual Sri Lanka passport — inclusion of children in a parent's passport is no longer permitted. Children's passport photos must meet the same technical specifications as adult photos. The child must be the only subject in the frame, with no hands, toys, car seats, or other people visible. For infants, closed eyes may be tolerated given the difficulty of keeping very young children alert, but open eyes are always preferred.

Common Reasons for Rejection

The most frequent reasons Sri Lanka passport photos are rejected by the Department of Immigration and Emigration include: wearing spectacles, shadows on the face or background, incorrect head size proportions, photo older than six months, non-uniform or patterned background, red-eye effect, poor print quality (inkjet or Polaroid prints), digital retouching or editing, and head tilting or turning.

Sri Lanka Visa Photo Requirements (2026)

Applying for a Sri Lanka visa — whether through the Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) system, a traditional visa application at a Sri Lankan embassy, or visa on arrival at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) — requires a compliant passport-style photograph. A non-compliant photo is one of the most common reasons for visa application delays and rejections. This complete guide covers all official Sri Lanka visa photo requirements for 2026 to help ensure your application is accepted the first time.

Photo Size and Dimensions

The Sri Lanka visa photo must measure exactly 35 mm × 45 mm (3.5 cm × 4.5 cm), the same standard biometric size used for the Sri Lanka passport. At 600 DPI, this equals approximately 413 × 531 pixels. Even minor deviations from these dimensions will result in automatic rejection — particularly for online ETA applications where the portal validates image dimensions programmatically. For digital submissions, the file must be in JPEG (JPG) format.

Background Requirements

The background must be plain white or very light-colored — white is the most recommended and universally accepted option. Light grey or cream backgrounds may be acceptable in some cases, but a pure white background eliminates any ambiguity. The background must be completely free of patterns, textures, objects, shadows, and gradients. Any colored, patterned, or busy background will result in immediate rejection. Ensure the background is evenly lit with no shadows cast by the subject behind them.

Face Size and Head Positioning

The face must be fully frontal, centered in the frame, and the head must occupy 70% to 80% of the total image height from the chin to the crown. The top of the shoulders should be visible at the bottom of the frame. The head must be straight — not tilted to either side, turned, or angled in any direction. Both ears should be visible. The full face from chin to forehead must appear within the frame with no cropping at any edge.

Facial Expression and Eyes

Maintain a neutral, relaxed facial expression — mouth closed, no smiling, no frowning, no raised or furrowed eyebrows. Both eyes must be fully open and looking directly at the camera. Eyebrows must not be raised or squinted. Red-eye in photos is not permitted; use appropriate lighting or red-eye correction during the shoot rather than digital post-processing. The face must be sharp, in focus, and clearly visible without any obstruction from hair, accessories, or shadows.

Photo Quality and Technical Specifications

The visa photo must be in full color — black-and-white images are not accepted. The image must be sharp, properly exposed, and free from pixelation, blur, or graininess. No digital filters, retouching, beauty enhancements, or color corrections are permitted. Lighting must be uniform across the entire face with no hot spots, harsh shadows, or uneven exposure. Natural skin tones must be accurately represented — over- or under-exposed skin tones will lead to rejection. For ETA online submissions, the file must be in JPEG format; file size requirements follow the ETA portal's validation rules, so ensure the image is high quality while staying within the upload limit. For physical visa applications at embassies or consulates, use professional-grade glossy or matte photo paper printed at an authorized photo studio.

Clothing and Accessories

Wear everyday clothing that clearly contrasts with the white background — avoid all-white or very light-colored tops as they can blend into the background and create compliance issues. Uniforms or clothing resembling military, official, or government attire are not permitted. Spectacles and glasses are strongly discouraged and should be removed for the photo. Sunglasses and tinted glasses are strictly prohibited under all circumstances. Head coverings are generally not permitted, with the exception of those worn for genuine religious reasons — in such cases, the full face from chin to forehead must remain clearly and fully visible with no shadows cast on the face. Avoid wearing heavy jewelry or large accessories that draw attention away from the face or cast shadows.

Sri Lanka ETA — Digital Photo Guidelines

The Sri Lanka Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is the primary visa pathway for most visitors in 2026 and is applied for online through the official Department of Immigration and Emigration portal. The ETA application requires uploading a passport-style color photograph in JPG format with a white background, neutral expression, and no glasses. The photo must accurately represent your current appearance. Poor quality photos or photos that do not meet the technical specifications are a leading cause of ETA processing delays. It is strongly recommended to have your photo professionally prepared and verified against the official requirements before uploading.

Photo Recency

All visa photos — whether for ETA, embassy applications, or visa on arrival — must have been taken within the last six months of the application or travel date. Photos older than six months will not be accepted. The photo must accurately reflect your current appearance, including current hair, any facial features, or significant changes in appearance since the photo was taken.

Children and Infants

Each child traveling to Sri Lanka, including newborns, must have their own individual visa application with a separate, individual photograph. The photo must show only the child — no hands, toys, car seats, supporting adults, or other objects should be visible. For infants, the same technical specifications apply; closed eyes may be tolerated for very young infants but open eyes are always preferred. The child's full face must be visible and centered in the frame.

Common Reasons for Sri Lanka Visa Photo Rejection

The most frequent reasons visa photos are rejected include: colored or patterned background, photo taken more than six months ago, wearing sunglasses or tinted glasses, digital editing or filters applied, shadows on the face or background, incorrect head-to-frame ratio, non-JPEG file format for online submissions, poor image resolution, smiling or non-neutral expression, and head tilted or turned away from the camera.

Quick Compliance Checklist

Before submitting your Sri Lanka visa application, verify the following: ✔ Photo size is exactly 35 × 45 mm ✔ Background is plain white or very light ✔ Head occupies 70–80% of image height ✔ Face is centered, straight, and fully visible ✔ Both eyes open, no red-eye ✔ Neutral expression, mouth closed ✔ No glasses, sunglasses, or non-religious head coverings ✔ Full color, no digital retouching or filters ✔ Photo taken within the last 6 months ✔ JPEG format for online ETA submission ✔ Clothing contrasts with the white background
