Tajikistan Passport Photo Requirements (2026)

Applying for or renewing a Tajikistan passport requires submitting photographs that strictly conform to the official biometric standards set by Tajikistan's passport authorities. Failing to meet even one requirement can result in your application being delayed or returned. This complete guide covers every official Tajikistan passport photo requirement for 2026 — from exact dimensions and background color to facial expression, clothing, and print quality.

Photo Size and Dimensions

The official Tajikistan passport photo size is 35 mm × 45 mm (3.5 cm × 4.5 cm), equivalent to approximately 1.37 × 1.77 inches. At a resolution of 600 DPI, this corresponds to 413 × 531 pixels. Applicants are required to submit four (4) identical photos with their passport application. Photos that do not conform precisely to these measurements will not be accepted. The photo must be printed on high-quality photo paper at a minimum resolution of 600 DPI — standard inkjet or laser prints are not suitable for submission.

Background Requirements

The background must be plain white with no shadows, patterns, gradients, or textures of any kind. The background must be uniformly lit and completely free of any objects, furniture, or other people. The applicant's clothing must contrast clearly with the white background — wearing white or very light-colored tops is strongly discouraged, as clothing that blends into the background can cause the photo to be rejected. A plain white wall or a clean white sheet (non-transparent) works well as a home background if a professional studio is unavailable.

Head Size and Positioning

The face — measured from the forehead edge to the bottom of the chin — must occupy 70% to 80% of the total photo height, with the head length from chin to forehead typically measuring between 31 mm and 36 mm within the 45 mm frame. The head must be perfectly centered within the photo. In the case of voluminous or large hairstyles, ensure that the entire head including the hairstyle is fully depicted within the frame without reducing the visible face size. The top of the shoulders must be visible at the lower portion of the image to provide proper framing context. The face must not be cut off at any edge of the photograph.

Facial Expression and Eyes

Maintain a neutral facial expression with your mouth closed. Smiling, frowning, raised eyebrows, squinting, or any non-neutral expression is not permitted. Both eyes must be fully open, clearly visible, and looking directly into the camera lens. There must be no hair, accessories, or shadows obscuring the eyes. Red-eye caused by camera flash must be avoided — use appropriate diffused lighting or an off-axis flash setup rather than post-processing corrections. The face must be in sharp focus with all facial features clearly distinguishable.

Lighting and Photo Quality

Lighting must be even and uniform across the entire face, with no harsh shadows on the cheeks, nose, chin, or forehead. Reflections on the face from direct flash must also be avoided. The photo must be in full color — black-and-white or monochrome photos are not accepted. The image must be sharp, properly exposed, and free from blur, pixelation, or graininess. No digital retouching, beauty filters, or color alterations are permitted. The skin tone must appear natural and true to life — both over-exposed (too light) and under-exposed (too dark) photos will be rejected.

Clothing and Accessories

Wear regular, everyday clothing for the photo. There is no specific dress code, but clothing must clearly contrast with the white background — avoid all-white or very light tops. Uniforms or clothing resembling military, police, or official government attire are not permitted. Headwear is generally not allowed; exceptions are made only for religious or cultural reasons, provided the full face remains clearly visible from chin to forehead with no shadows cast on the face. Glasses must be removed for Tajikistan passport photos — spectacles are not permitted regardless of prescription or medical need. Beards are permitted provided they represent the applicant's everyday appearance and do not significantly obscure facial features.

Photo Recency

Tajikistan passport photos must have been taken within the last six months of the application date. Photos older than six months are considered outdated and will not be accepted. The photo must accurately reflect your current appearance — significant changes in appearance (such as weight changes, new facial hair, or changed hairstyle) since the photo was taken may require a new photo to be submitted.

Infants and Children

Infants and children must have their own individual passport photo meeting the same technical specifications as adults. The photo must show only the child — no hands, toys, car seats, or other adults may appear in the frame. Photographing infants from above in a lying-down position is acceptable, provided a white sheet is placed underneath to achieve the required white background. The infant's headwear and pacifier must be removed before taking the photo. The child's full face must be visible and centered within the frame.

Common Reasons for Rejection

The most frequent reasons Tajikistan passport photos are rejected include: glasses not removed, shadows on the face or background, head not centered or tilted, photo older than six months, background that is not plain white, clothing that blends into the background, red-eye effect, digital retouching or filters applied, head or hairstyle cut off at the edges, and insufficient print resolution or quality.

Where to Apply

Tajikistan passport applications are processed through the Ministry of Internal Affairs (passportization departments) at regional offices across Tajikistan, as well as through Tajikistan diplomatic missions abroad. When applying at overseas embassies or consulates, four compliant printed photographs must accompany the application along with all required supporting documents.

Tajikistan Visa Photo Requirements (2026)

Tajikistan operates a three-tier visa system in 2026: visa-free access for select CIS nationals, an electronic visa (e-visa) system through the official portal at evisa.tj for most OECD and ASEAN nationals, and embassy-issued visas for all other nationalities. Importantly, the photo requirements differ between the Tajikistan passport and the Tajikistan e-visa — the e-visa uses a larger photo format. This guide covers all official photo requirements for both visa types to help ensure your application is accepted without delays.

Tajikistan E-Visa Photo Size — Important Difference

Unlike the passport photo, the Tajikistan e-visa photo has a different, larger format: 50 mm × 60 mm (5 cm × 6 cm), equivalent to approximately 1.97 × 2.36 inches. At 600 DPI this corresponds to 1181 × 1417 pixels. This is a critical distinction — submitting a 35×45 mm passport-format photo for the e-visa application may result in rejection at the evisa.tj portal. The digital file must be in JPEG format with a maximum file size of 240 KB and a minimum resolution of 300 DPI. Only one photo needs to be uploaded for the online e-visa application.

Embassy Visa Photo Size

For applicants applying for a Tajikistan visa in person at a Tajikistan embassy or consulate abroad, the standard 35 mm × 45 mm passport-format photo applies. Four printed photos are typically required alongside the completed visa application form and supporting documents including a valid passport, proof of accommodation, and (for some nationalities) an invitation letter or confirmed itinerary.

Background Requirements

For both e-visa and embassy visa applications, the background must be plain white — uniform, smooth, and entirely free of patterns, gradients, textures, shadows, or any other objects. The applicant's clothing must contrast clearly with the white background. Off-white, cream, grey, or any colored background will result in the photo being rejected. Ensure the background is evenly and uniformly lit to prevent shadows forming behind the subject.

Head Size and Facial Framing

The face — from the forehead edge to the bottom of the chin — must occupy 70% to 80% of the total image height. For the e-visa 50×60 mm format, the minimum head height is 45 mm within the 60 mm frame, with the top of the head positioned a minimum of 3.6 mm from the top edge of the photo. The head must be centered, straight, and looking directly forward. The full face from chin to crown must be visible within the frame with no cropping at any edge. The top of the shoulders must be visible at the bottom of the image.

Facial Expression and Eyes

A neutral, relaxed facial expression is required — mouth closed, no smiling, no frowning, no raised eyebrows. Both eyes must be fully open, clearly visible, and looking directly at the camera. Eyes must not be squinted, partially closed, or obscured by hair or accessories. Red-eye is not permitted — use diffused or off-camera lighting during the shoot to prevent red-eye rather than applying digital corrections afterward.

Photo Quality and Technical Standards

The photo must be in full color with natural, accurate skin tone representation. The image must be sharp, in focus, and free from blur, pixelation, or graininess. No digital retouching, beauty filters, brightness adjustments, or color corrections are permitted. Lighting must be uniform across the entire face — no harsh shadows on the cheeks, nose, chin, or forehead, and no reflective glare from direct flash. For the online e-visa upload, use JPEG format, ensure a minimum resolution of 300 DPI, and keep the file size under 240 KB.

Clothing and Accessories

Wear your regular, everyday clothing for the visa photo. Clothing must clearly contrast with the white background — avoid all-white or very light-colored tops that may blend into the background. Uniforms or attire resembling official, military, or government dress are not permitted. Glasses must be removed for the photo. Headwear is not permitted except for verified religious or cultural reasons, in which case the full face from chin to forehead must remain clearly visible with no shadows cast on any facial feature. Beards are acceptable if they represent the applicant's natural everyday appearance.

How to Apply for the Tajikistan E-Visa in 2026

The Tajikistan e-visa is applied for entirely online through the official portal at evisa.tj. The application requires uploading a compliant face photo (50×60 mm, JPEG, under 240 KB) and a scanned color copy of the passport data page. The processing fee is approximately USD 30 base fee plus USD 20 processing fee. Standard processing takes 1 to 3 working days. The e-visa is valid for 90 days from the date of issue, with a maximum stay of 60 days. Applicants are advised to print two copies of the approved e-visa to present at the border. The e-visa is accepted at all airports and designated land border crossings. Note: travelers intending to visit the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Oblast (GBAO) — including the Pamir Highway — must also obtain a separate GBAO permit, which can be added to the e-visa application for an additional USD 20–30.

Photo Recency

Visa photos must have been taken within the last six months of the application date. This applies to both e-visa digital uploads and physical photos submitted at embassies. The photo must accurately reflect your current appearance at the time of application.

Common Reasons for Tajikistan Visa Photo Rejection

Frequent rejection reasons include: using a 35×45 mm photo for the e-visa instead of the required 50×60 mm format, file size exceeding 240 KB, non-JPEG file format, colored or non-white background, shadows on the face or background, wearing glasses, red-eye, digital retouching or filters, head tilted or not centered, photo older than six months, and clothing color blending into the white background.

Quick Compliance Checklist

Before submitting your Tajikistan visa application, verify: ✔ E-visa photo is 50×60 mm (not 35×45 mm) ✔ Embassy visa photo is 35×45 mm ✔ Background is plain white, no shadows ✔ Head occupies 70–80% of image height ✔ Face centered, straight, looking forward ✔ Both eyes open, no red-eye ✔ Neutral expression, mouth closed ✔ Glasses removed ✔ No non-religious headwear ✔ Full color, no retouching or filters ✔ Photo taken within 6 months ✔ JPEG format, under 240 KB, min 300 DPI for e-visa upload

name: Belgium Passport
passportcontent:
Belgium Passport Photo: Official Requirements for 2026

The FPS Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation — Belgium's federal authority for consular services — states clearly on its official diplomatie.belgium.be portal: your passport photo must comply with ICAO standards (International Civil Aviation Organization). These standards are stricter than in the past, and if your photo doesn't comply, your municipality will refuse it outright. The photo measures 35 × 45 mm, sits on a light grey background, and must be no older than 6 months.

Belgium Passport Photo — Technical Specifications

Size
35 × 45 mm
Background
Light Grey
Head Height
31–36 mm
Standard
ICAO 9303
Recency
≤ 6 Months
Format
Color / Print
Quantity
1 Photo
Validity
7 Years

The Four Fundamental Rules from FPS Foreign Affairs

The official quality-requirements page lists four rules you must follow when your photo is taken, and each one carries real weight at the counter:

  • Neutral facial expression: mouth shut, no smiling.
  • Head and shoulders straight, positioned right in front of the camera.
  • Face totally uncovered: your forehead, chin, and the area toward your ears must all be visible.
  • Eyes perfectly visible: no reflecting or tinted glasses; frames must not be too big, yet not sit too close to the eyeline either.

FPS Foreign Affairs adds a practical tip that removes a common failure point entirely: if you wear glasses, you can simply take them off for the photo — even if you wear them every day. This sidesteps glare, tinted lenses, and frame-obstruction issues in one step.

Head Position and Face Visibility

Face the camera directly, with your head and shoulders straight — never tilt or turn your head to a three-quarter angle. Your face stays fully uncovered from forehead to chin, and the skin toward your ears remains visible on both sides. Hair must not fall across your eyebrows or eyes, and long fringes should be pinned back so the entire facial oval reads clearly in the frame.

Head Size and Framing

Within the 35 × 45 mm frame, your head — measured from the top of the hair to the bottom of the chin — falls between roughly 31 mm and 36 mm, leaving a small margin above the crown and space on both sides of the face. Your neck and the upper part of your shoulders stay visible too, giving the reviewing official a full, unobstructed view for identity verification.

Glasses, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Glasses are discouraged rather than banned outright: the lenses must never be tinted or reflective, and the frame must neither obscure your eyes nor sit awkwardly close to the eyeline. Since this rule trips up many applicants, FPS Foreign Affairs recommends removing glasses for the photo entirely. Head coverings aren't permitted except for religious reasons, and even then your face must remain fully visible from forehead to chin.

Background, Lighting, and Print Quality

The background stays light and uniform — commonly light grey, though a very light cream or pale blue is also accepted — with no shadows falling on the face or the backdrop. The photo must be in color; black-and-white prints are no longer accepted. Submit an original print, not a photocopy, taken no earlier than six months before your application. If you print from a digital file, the resolution must reach a minimum of 400 dpi so the image stays sharp at actual size.

Where the Photo Gets Checked

You submit your passport application, along with the required photo, at your local municipality (commune/gemeente) in Belgium or at a Belgian embassy or consulate abroad. The photo shows your face straight on, with head and shoulders positioned directly in front of the camera — the same neutral-expression standard FPS Foreign Affairs applies to passport photos carries over to visa photos. Create Estonia Passport Photo: The Complete 2025 Guide

The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) rejects thousands of Estonian passport applications every year because of non-compliant photos. A single mistake — the wrong background, a tilted head, or an outdated image — can delay your passport by weeks. This guide walks you through every official requirement so you get it right the first time.

Photo Dimensions and Digital Specifications

Estonia enforces strict technical standards for passport photos, whether you print them or upload them to the self-service portal.

  • Print size: 35mm x 45mm (413 x 531 pixels at 300 DPI).
  • Digital upload minimum: at least 1,300 x 1,600 pixels.
  • File size: between 1MB and 5MB for digital submissions.
  • Color: full color only — black-and-white photos are not accepted.
  • Editing: the photo must remain unedited. Do not retouch skin, remove blemishes, or apply filters.
  • Source: scanned photos and screenshots from a computer or phone screen are strictly prohibited.

Background Requirements

Use a plain, light-colored background with no texture, pattern, gradient, or shadow. Light grey is the standard choice, though any single light tone works if it contrasts clearly with your hair and skin. Remove furniture, doors, and other objects from the frame, and make sure no shadow falls on the wall behind you.

Face Size and Positioning

Center your face in the frame and keep your head straight — do not tilt it left, right, forward, or back. Your face should fill 70-80% of the photo height, measured from chin to crown. Look directly into the lens with both eyes level and fully open; the camera should sit at eye level, not above or below.

Expression Rules

Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed. Smiling, frowning, or raising your eyebrows can cause rejection. Relax your shoulders and face the camera squarely rather than at an angle.

Glasses and Headwear

Estonia generally advises against wearing glasses in passport photos. If you must wear them for medical reasons, remove sunglasses and tinted lenses entirely, and make sure the frames never cover your eyes. Avoid any glare or reflection on the lenses — reposition your lighting or remove the glasses if reflections persist. Headwear, hats, and headphones are not permitted, except for religious head coverings, which must not obscure any part of your face from the forehead to the chin.

Lighting Quality

Use soft, even lighting from the front so no shadows fall across your face, neck, or the background. Avoid harsh overhead light, which creates dark patches under the eyes and nose, and avoid backlighting, which darkens your face while overexposing the background.

Where to Take Your Passport Photo

You have three official options in Estonia:

  • Photo booth at a PPA service office: Every service office offers a free digital photo booth, even if you're not submitting your application there. The photo is stored digitally and can be reused for 183 days for applications submitted at any service office or through the self-service portal (weapons permits are excluded from this option). While in the booth, you can also provide fingerprints and a signature sample if your application requires them.
  • Photographer's studio: A professional photographer familiar with Estonian document standards can guarantee compliant lighting, background, and framing in a single visit.
  • Self-taken photo: You may photograph yourself and upload the image to the self-service portal, but it must strictly follow every rule in this guide and must not be older than six months.

If you took your photo in a service office booth but plan to submit your application by email, mention this in your application. When emailing the photo, include the applicant's first name, surname, and personal identification number or date of birth in the message body so the PPA can match it to your record.

Special Instructions for Young Children (0-7 Years)

Photographing a young child is harder than photographing an adult, and Estonia adjusts its guidance accordingly.

  • Book a session at a photographer's studio when possible — professionals are better equipped to capture a compliant image quickly.
  • Photo booths often fail with young children because they can't hold still and face the camera long enough. If you must use a booth, ask a PPA official for assistance.
  • Use a plain, light, single-color background with no patterns or objects.
  • The child must look straight into the camera with a closed mouth.
  • Remove large hair accessories, bows, and any toys or objects from the frame.
  • As with adults, scans and screen screenshots are not accepted, and the photo must be unedited.

How to Photograph Yourself Correctly

If you're taking the photo without professional help, ask a family member, friend, or acquaintance to help you. Use the rear camera of a smartphone rather than the front-facing camera — front cameras use a wider lens that distorts facial proportions and can cause the photo to be rejected. Stand about two meters from a plain wall in a well-lit room, ideally near a window with diffused daylight, and have the photographer stand at your eye level.

Common Mistakes That Cause Rejection

  • Submitting a photo older than six months (self-taken) or older than 183 days (photo booth).
  • Using a colored, patterned, or shadowed background.
  • Wearing sunglasses, tinted lenses, or a hat without religious grounds.
  • Tilting the head or looking away from the camera.
  • Applying filters, cropping tightly, or editing skin tone.
  • Submitting a scanned print or a screenshot instead of an original digital file.

Before You Submit

Run through this quick checklist before uploading or printing your photo: correct pixel dimensions and file size, plain light background, neutral expression, centered and level face, no headwear or glare, and a file that has not been edited. A non-compliant photo extends processing time, so a few extra minutes of care now saves you weeks later.

Create Estonia Visa Photo : What You Need to Know

An Estonian visa photo follows the same core standards as a passport photo, but the submission process and validity rules differ slightly depending on where and how you apply. This guide covers the technical specifications, composition rules, and practical steps for getting a compliant visa photo, whether you're applying at an embassy, a consulate, or through the online portal.

Technical Specifications

Your visa photo must meet the same measurable standards used for Estonian passports.

  • Standard print size: 35mm x 45mm (413 x 531 pixels at 300 DPI).
  • Digital submission minimum: at least 1,300 x 1,600 pixels.
  • File size: between 1MB and 5MB when uploading digitally.
  • Color format: full color, never black-and-white.
  • No editing: the photo must be an unedited, unaltered original.
  • No scans or screenshots: a scanned print or a screenshot of a phone or computer screen is not accepted under any circumstances.

Background and Lighting

Photograph yourself against a plain, light, single-color background — light grey works best — with no shadows, patterns, or objects visible behind you. Light the face evenly from the front so no shadows fall across your cheeks, nose, or the background wall. Avoid strong side lighting, overhead lighting, and backlit setups, all of which distort skin tone and obscure facial features that visa officers need to see clearly.

Head Position and Face Size

Center your face in the frame and keep your head level — no tilting forward, backward, or to either side. Your face must occupy 70-80% of the photo's total height, measured from your chin to the top of your head. Look directly at the camera with both eyes open and level with one another.

Expression and Posture

Keep your expression neutral, with your mouth closed and your face relaxed. Do not smile, frown, or raise your eyebrows. Square your shoulders to the camera rather than turning at an angle, since an angled pose can distort the perceived proportions of your face.

Glasses and Head Coverings

Remove glasses whenever possible for a visa photo. If you need them for medical reasons, take off sunglasses or tinted lenses entirely, and make sure the frames don't cover your eyes and don't cast glare or reflections. Hats, headphones, and other headwear are not permitted, with one exception: religious head coverings are allowed as long as they leave your entire face, from forehead to chin, fully visible.

Adults vs. Children: Different Rules Apply

For adults, follow every requirement above precisely, using the rear camera of a smartphone (never the front camera, which distorts facial proportions) if you're photographing yourself at home. Ask someone else to take the picture for you and stand roughly two meters from a plain, evenly lit wall.

For children aged 0-7, Estonia recommends visiting a photographer's studio instead of a self-service photo booth, since young children often can't hold still long enough for a booth to capture a usable image. If a studio isn't available, a PPA official can assist with a booth photo. Children's photos must show a straight gaze into the camera with a closed mouth, a plain light background, and no large hair accessories or toys in frame.

Where to Get Your Visa Photo Taken

  • PPA service office photo booth: Free to use, even if you're not filing your application at that location. The digital photo remains valid for 183 days and can be reused across service offices or the self-service portal, with the exception of weapons permit applications.
  • Professional photographer: A studio experienced with Estonian visa and passport standards can produce a compliant photo in one sitting, which is especially useful if you're on a tight visa appointment timeline.
  • Self-taken photo: Acceptable for upload to the self-service portal, provided it is no older than six months and meets every requirement listed above.

Submitting by Email

If you took your photo at a service office booth but are submitting your visa application by email, note this explicitly in your application. Include the applicant's first name, surname, and either their personal identification number or date of birth in the email body so the office can correctly match the photo to the file.

Mistakes That Delay Visa Processing

  • Using a photo older than the six-month (self-taken) or 183-day (photo booth) validity window.
  • Submitting a scanned or screenshotted image instead of an original digital file.
  • Wearing tinted glasses, a hat, or headphones without a religious exemption.
  • Uneven lighting that creates shadows on the face or background.
  • A tilted head, closed eyes, or an off-center face.
  • Editing or retouching the image, including cropping that changes the required proportions.

Final Check Before You Apply

Before attaching your photo to a visa application, confirm the file size and pixel dimensions match the requirements, the background is plain and light, your expression is neutral, your head is level and centered, and the image is a genuine, unedited digital file. Taking a few extra minutes to verify these details helps you avoid the processing delays that come with a rejected photo.

Spain Passport Photo Requirements: Complete 2026 Guide

Applying for a Spanish passport? Your photo must follow strict rules set by the Spanish government. A single mistake in size, background, or expression can delay your application by weeks. This guide covers every Spain passport photo requirement in detail, so you submit a compliant photo on the first try.

Spain Passport Photo Size

The official Spain passport photo size is 30mm x 40mm (354 x 472 pixels at 300 DPI). This size photo spain uses is smaller than the US passport standard, so avoid reusing photos taken for other countries. Print your photo at the exact spain passport photo size before submission, since oversized or undersized prints are rejected at application centers in Madrid, Barcelona, and consulates worldwide.

SpecificationRequirement
Physical size30mm x 40mm
Digital resolution354 x 472 pixels
Print DPI300
BackgroundPlain white
Face height70% – 80% of frame

Background Requirements

Your background must be a plain, uniform white with no shadows, patterns, or texture. Avoid colored walls, furniture, or busy rooms. Uneven lighting behind you often creates gray patches that officials flag as non-compliant, so photograph against a flat, evenly lit white surface.

Face and Head Positioning

Your face must fill 70% to 80% of the total photo height, measured from chin to crown. Center your head in the frame and look directly at the camera with your head straight, not tilted. Officials measure this ratio precisely, so a passport photo editor that automatically crops to spec saves you from manual guesswork.

Eyes and Expression

Keep both eyes fully open and visible, positioned between 50% and 70% of the frame height. Use a neutral expression: mouth closed, no smiling, and a relaxed face. Do not tilt your head or squint, since asymmetry is one of the most common rejection reasons for a spanish passport picture.

Glasses and Headwear Rules

Glasses are generally not allowed unless required for medical reasons, and even then, frames must never obscure your eyes and lenses must show no glare or reflection. Headwear is prohibited except for religious reasons, and any permitted headwear must not hide your hairline, ears, or facial features.

Lighting and Image Quality

Lighting must be even across your entire face, with no shadows under the eyes, nose, or chin. Use diffused, front-facing light instead of a single overhead bulb. The final image should be sharp, in true color, and free from red-eye, blur, or digital artifacts.

How to Create a Compliant Photo Online

You don't need a professional studio to meet these standards. PixPassVisa's spain passport photo maker lets you upload any selfie or photo, then automatically crops, resizes, and adjusts the background to match the official 30mm x 40mm specification.   2. Let the tool detect your face and crop it to the required proportions.
  3. Review the automatic background removal and whitening.
  4. Download your photo sized for printing or digital submission.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Submitting a photo sized for a different country's passport.
  • Wearing glasses, hats, or headphones in the frame.
  • Using a shadowed or off-white background.
  • Smiling or tilting the head instead of a neutral, straight pose.
  • Printing at the wrong DPI, which blurs facial features.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the exact spain passport photo size? The required size is 30mm x 40mm, equal to 354 x 472 pixels at 300 DPI.

Can I take my own photo at home? Yes. Use a plain white wall, natural front lighting, and a photo editing tool to crop and format it to spec.

Do glasses disqualify my photo? Yes, unless worn for medical reasons, and even then no glare or obstruction is allowed.

How recent must the photo be? Spanish authorities require photos taken within the last six months to reflect your current appearance.

Face Positioning for Visa Photos

Center your face in the frame so it covers 70% to 80% of the total photo height. Keep your head straight and your shoulders level, facing the camera directly. This proportion applies to every visa category, from tourist visas to long-term residency permits.

Eyes, Expression, and Pose

Both eyes must stay open and clearly visible, positioned within 50% to 70% of the frame height. Maintain a neutral expression with your mouth closed and no exaggerated features. A relaxed, natural pose without smiling or frowning helps your photo match biometric standards used during visa processing.

Glasses, Headwear, and Accessories

Remove glasses unless you have a documented medical need, and never let frames cover your eyes or reflect glare. Headwear is not permitted except for religious observance, and it must never conceal your face outline, hairline, or ears. Remove hats, headphones, and large jewelry before your photo is taken.

Digital and Print Formats Accepted
